findings_plain_language: Executor gap found: the pinned kernel refuses six registry source types outright (BOUND_CAPABILITY_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED). 16 of the 66 bound capabilities - every python repair loop, the chart readers, the tesseract OCR binding, the acceptance controllers - could never run through the one entry, although #4707 had counted them as reachable. The entry now runs those adapters itself (E1): same adapter file, same arguments, same expectation check as the kernel, declared stdlib modules verified first, execution rows marked FRONT_LAYER_LOCAL_ADAPTER_EXECUTION_V1, and R5/R6 still apply on top.

Nine more capability shapes are measured end to end with stdlib-only checkers. Code capabilities for the first time: the test-guided repair loop and the strict-progress repair loop propose a unified diff for a fresh injected bug (flipped operator in one of three functions); the checker applies the diff itself and re-runs the tests in a separate interpreter with bytecode caching disabled - 50/50 and 50/50. The dynamic fault localizer ranks the buggy function first in 50/50 fresh modules.
Declared non-authority honoured: the repair loops restore the source after proposing the patch (NO_SOURCE_WRITE_OR_PROMOTION_AUTHORITY); the checker fails any run that wrote into the source.

Real limits found (recorded, pinned files untouched): (a) the fault localizer passes its own argv to the traced test script, so unittest.main()-style tests cannot be localized - its declared input class is plain assert scripts, which is what the generator writes; (b) the strict-progress loop needs unittest's 'FAILED (failures=N)' line to measure progress, so it gets a unittest file; (c) the sqlite verifier requires a capability_id column and the apt sqlite3 binary.
msgpack through the npm library decodes correctly with the hand-written reader 50/50; the BSON reader is in place for the runner.

A false-pass trap in my own checker was found and closed: a stale __pycache__ of an earlier candidate can answer for a differently patched module of equal size written within the same second; the checker now uses a fresh directory and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE.
